gaps.sentence: The temple is thought ___ (build) more than two thousand years ago.
gaps.explanation: Perfect passive infinitive: to have been + built for an event earlier than the main verb.

gaps.sentence: Your contract will ___ for a further twelve months.
gaps.explanation: After 'will', passive = be + past participle: will be renewed.

gaps.sentence: This wall ___ (build) centuries ago — no modern tool leaves marks like these.
gaps.explanation: Perfect modal passive: must have been + built to draw a conclusion about the past.

gaps.sentence: The stolen car ___ (find) abandoned in a car park this morning.
gaps.explanation: 'This morning' (now over) takes past simple passive: was + found.

gaps.sentence: The debt ___ (repay) in full by May, he promised.
gaps.explanation: Reported future passive: would be + past participle after a past reporting verb.

gaps.sentence: The decision ___ (announce) at yesterday's press conference.
gaps.explanation: 'Yesterday' signals past simple passive: was + announced.

gaps.sentence: By the time you read this, the treaty ___ (sign) by all twelve delegations.
gaps.explanation: 'By the time + present clause' with a future meaning takes the future perfect passive.

gaps.sentence: Thousands of homes ___ (flood) when the river burst its banks.
gaps.explanation: Past simple passive: were + flooded. The cause (the river) is in the when-clause.
